I traced the issue and recorded the findings in [.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md). This fault-localization role did not permit project source or test edits.

The controller version floor is currently 3.10 in [the CLI](/app/lib/ansible/cli/__init__.py:14), [package metadata](/app/setup.cfg:40), and [ansible-test’s version list](/app/test/lib/ansible_test/_util/target/common/constants.py:12). [ansible-test’s entry point](/app/bin/ansible-test:25) also uses a different user-facing error. The explicit requirement calls for a 3.12 floor, although the issue title only specifies dropping 3.10; the coordinated change should follow the explicit 3.12 requirement.

[Collection installation](/app/lib/ansible/galaxy/collection/__init__.py:1605) creates the prohibited private tar cache. [_extract_tar_dir](/app/lib/ansible/galaxy/collection/__init__.py:1690) strips the incoming directory suffix and reads that cache. Its [existing tests](/app/test/units/cli/galaxy/test_collection_extract_tar.py:13) encode the old behavior, so a fix needs to cover direct `getmember(dirname)`, unchanged input, and the exact missing-member error.

The `reload_module` import already exists behind a legacy fallback in [the collection finder](/app/lib/ansible/utils/collection_loader/_collection_finder.py:35). Its `string_types` checks are the likely target of the ambiguous “insistence … str” requirement. Older-version compatibility also appears in [importlib resources](/app/lib/ansible/compat/importlib_resources.py:10) and [dependency constraints](/app/test/lib/ansible_test/_data/requirements/constraints.txt:4). Controller cleanup should preserve compatibility needed for remote-node Python versions.
